clue.text: Cockney's toiletry should alleviate perspiration

definitions.note: describes a cooling machine by what it is for, so it stands for the noun

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker famously drops the aitch at the start of words, so the opening H goes

parts.note: a hair conditioner is a toiletry used after shampoo

explanation.surface: An advert claims a Cockney's bathroom product will stop you sweating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney's' tells you to say the word as a Londoner of the East End would, dropping the initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooling appliance chills a room and so stops people sweating.

clue.text: Someone from Greenland wearing formal clothing? Not at first

parts.note: someone wearing clothes is in them

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for formal clothing is not there

parts.note: a suit is formal clothing

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Greenlander might be dressed up in formal wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing formal clothing' reads as describing the Greenlander, but splits into two pieces; 'Not at first' beheads the clothing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous Arctic people include the native population of Greenland.

clue.text: Yellow and black bird about to be displayed first

indicators.note: says the short word for about is shown before the bird rather than after it

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
a raven is a large black bird

explanation.surface: Describes a yellow and black bird showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow and black' looks like a bird's colouring; 'Yellow' alone is the definition, in its sense of cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and craven means lacking courage.

clue.text: See red with one disorganised and thoroughly feckless person?

indicators.note: the letters of red and one are put into disorder, giving a new arrangement

parts.note: doing something well means doing it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage at a messy, idle good-for-nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorganised' turns RED and ONE into NEERDO; 'See' is only a link word pointing the solver at the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout who never does anything useful is a classic idle, worthless type.

clue.text: Part of the Cypriot alphabet

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the run of letters across Cypriot alphabet

explanation.surface: Points to one letter of the alphabet used in Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'CypriOT Alphabet', and Cyprus uses the Greek alphabet, so the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek is spoken in Cyprus, and this is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Long to follow up short pieces, in verse

definitions.text: Long to follow up short pieces, in verse

parts.words: Long to follow up short pieces, in verse
parts.note: a metrical foot of a short syllable followed by a long one; lines built of such feet

explanation.definitionFit: Verse written in feet where an unstressed syllable precedes a stressed one, short then long.

clue.text: Eating to get restored energy, given treat

indicators.note: the letters of eating to are put back together in a fresh order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dieter eats to regain strength after a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges EATING TO into NEGOTIAT, then E for energy is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat with someone is to bargain or discuss terms with them.

clue.text: Think very hard, revealing personal intelligence under torture

indicators.note: in a down clue the words for personal intelligence sit below the word for torture

parts.note: the rack was an instrument of torture
one's means belonging to oneself, personal
brains means intelligence

explanation.surface: A victim reveals private secrets while being tortured.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to strain your mind trying to remember or solve something.

clue.text: "To sleep: perchance to dream: - - "

parts.note: the gap is the words that complete this line from Hamlet's 'To be or not to be' speech

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Hamlet continues the line with this phrase, meaning that is the snag.

clue.text: Second person with appeal about to call for whatever's needed

indicators.note: the second person and appeal go round the outside of the word for call

parts.note: you is the second person pronoun
it means sex appeal, as in the It girl
to name is to call

explanation.surface: Someone attractive phones a friend to ask what is required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with appeal' sounds like charm, but 'appeal' here is the old slang 'It' for sex appeal; 'about' wraps the two outer pieces round the word for call.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means anything at all, every item one might want.

clue.text: Wise men about to produce something marvellous

parts.note: the Magi were the three wise men of the Nativity
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: The three kings are about to perform a wonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is sorcery or wonder, anything enchanting.

clue.text: Someone rash involved in striking match

definitions.meaning: the tip of a match grows hot when it is struck

explanation.surface: An impulsive player gets caught up in a strike-bound fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: An impetuous person acts without thinking; a struck match has a heated tip.

clue.text: Small restaurant using right ingredient in manufactured gravy

indicators.note: the letter for right becomes one of the components inside the gravy brand

parts.note: Bisto is a long-standing British brand of gravy granules

explanation.surface: A café makes its gravy with the proper ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: BISTO is a British brand of factory-made gravy powder; R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a modest café or eating place, originally French.

clue.text: You and I on a long walk in Yorkshire area, once

parts.note: you and I together make we
striding means walking with long steps

explanation.surface: Two friends hike across the Yorkshire countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was once split into three administrative divisions called Ridings; this was one of them until 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic administrative division of the northern English county, abolished in 1974.

clue.text: Extract from "triffic" piece of music

indicators.note: the answer is a run of letters taken out of the word triffic

explanation.surface: Quotes a slangy word of praise for a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: In rock and jazz this is a short repeated phrase or melody.

clue.text: So eggs may be items supermarket's giving away?

definitions.meaning: describing eggs laid by hens allowed to roam outdoors
a range of goods offered at no charge

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a supermarket's handouts might be eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs from outdoor-roaming hens carry this label; a shop's product line offered gratis fits the second sense.

clue.text: Cries, receiving post about a gamble

indicators.note: the word for post goes around the outside of the word for cries

parts.note: a stake is a post driven into the ground
weeps means cries

explanation.surface: Someone sobs on receiving a letter about a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, so the post wraps the cries; 'receiving' only joins the pieces, and 'a gamble' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery-style bet where the winner takes all the pooled money.

clue.text: Particular work to be done in a field

definitions.text: Particular work to be done in a field

parts.words: Particular work to be done in a field
parts.note: suggests farm labour, but means the special skill someone has in their field of expertise

explanation.definitionFit: A person's particular area of expertise is the work they focus on in their profession.

clue.text: Popular garden plant available

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
stock is a scented garden flower

explanation.surface: A popular garden flower is on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods a shop holds on its shelves ready for sale can be bought now.

clue.text: To try and provide examples of this

definitions.text: To try and provide examples of this

parts.words: To try and provide examples of this
parts.note: read as an attempt to give examples, but 'to try' and 'to provide' are each a doing word

explanation.definitionFit: Words like 'try' and 'provide' are action words, a part of speech in grammar.

clue.text: Fuss about a soldier being slow

indicators.note: the word for fuss goes round the outside of a and the soldier

parts.note: ado means fuss
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier dawdling causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this tempo marking means at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Has to go round like a 12, endlessly in distress

indicators.note: the word has is placed around the outside of the other piece
the last letter of the word for like a 12 is cut off

parts.note: 12 across is someone rash, so like one is rash

explanation.surface: A hothead in trouble is surrounded by people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like a 12' points to 12 across, someone rash; 'endlessly' trims its final letter, and 'to go round' puts the remainder inside the clue word 'Has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass is to trouble or torment someone repeatedly.

clue.text: Jones may be in a state…

definitions.meaning: ... Jones is the film archaeologist played by Harrison Ford
one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest

explanation.surface: Someone named Jones is in a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a state' reads as being upset; 'in' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The adventurer of the films takes his first name from a Midwestern US state.

clue.text: Regular starter for the oaks?

parts.note: sounds like a racehorse running in the Oaks, but means the seed from which every oak tree begins

explanation.definitionFit: Every oak tree grows from this nut, so it always gets one going.

clue.text: First in line doesn't appear to be competent

indicators.note: points to the opening letter of the word for line
that opening letter is missing from the result

parts.note: a cable is a line, as in a telegraph line

explanation.surface: The person at the front of the queue fails to show up, which seems efficient.
explanation.walkthrough: CABLE loses its first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable, having the skill to do something.

clue.text: …and not backing the same music

indicators.note: means the word for and not runs from right to left

parts.note: nor means and not
do is short for ditto, the same

explanation.surface: Continues the previous clue: Jones is not reversing the same tune.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 23 across, so 'and' belongs to this clue; 'backing' turns the word for 'and not' round, and DO is short for ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form with a recurring main theme.

clue.text: Fetch a bit of fluff, appearing humble

parts.note: to fetch is to bring
down is soft fluffy feathers

explanation.surface: A dog fetches a fluffy toy, looking meek.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone is to lower or humiliate them.

clue.text: Banker we re-employed worked hard to innovate

indicators.note: the letters of banker we are put to work again in a new order

parts.note: ground, as in ground away, means worked hard

explanation.surface: A rehired banker toils away at fresh ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To pioneer is to do something never done before.
